small_guidance:
- The inner loop recomputes weights for every (n, hw_block, od); since weights are tiny (OC*IC*KD*KH*KW = 24*3*27 = 1944 floats), preload the entire weight tensor once per program into registers/SMEM and reuse across all OD iterations and the OC×HW outer product.
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_HW (e.g. 256/512 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3) and try num_stages=3-4 to better hide the long inner-loop latency; key on (OH*OW) only since OC/KD/KH/KW are fixed.
- Reorder the OD/IC/KD loops so the OD dimension reuses overlapping x rows: along OD, the x window shifts by one HW plane per step, so caching the partial sum per kd or fusing OD into the kd loop (sliding-window) can cut x loads roughly KD×.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, HW-tile), with the K dimension being IC*KD*KH*KW (=81). Load the small weight matrix [OC, K] once into SMEM, then issue a single tl.dot per OD step against an [K, BLOCK_HW] gathered patch — this replaces the scalar FMA outer-product loop with tensor-core mma.
- Make the OD loop the outermost reduction axis kept in registers: maintain min_acc[OC, BLOCK_HW] across OD, and for each od compute the conv tile via tl.dot. Fuse the channel softmax epilogue (max → exp → sum → divide) on the resident [OC, BLOCK_HW] tile, exactly as now, so output is written once.
- Consider channels-last input layout (N, D, H, W, IC) so the K-axis gather is contiguous in IC and KW, enabling vectorized loads; alternatively, since IC=3 is tiny, pad IC to 4 and treat (IC, KW) as the inner contiguous chunk to enable 128-bit loads.
